items.titel: Qatar Grand Prix was ‘right decision’ despite regional tensions: MotoGP
items.anriss: MotoGP chief says 'it was normal that the riders showed their concerns' but was surprised at Yamaha's ⁠⁠⁠⁠withdrawal.

absaetze.t: MotoGP chief says ‘it was normal that the riders showed their concerns’ but was surprised at Yamaha’s ⁠withdrawal.

MotoGP’s deputy chief Carlos Ezpeleta says the ‌‌‌‌championship was right to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix despite rider concerns about travelling to the Gulf amid the United States-Israel war on ⁠⁠⁠⁠Iran, but added that Yamaha’s ⁠⁠⁠⁠withdrawal came as a surprise.
MotoGP had based its decision on official information from the Qatari government and from embassies with a large presence in the paddock, Ezpeleta revealed on Wednesday.
The race was postponed from April to November 6–8 due to the regional conflict, and ⁠⁠⁠⁠Ezpeleta said the event would have been cancelled or postponed again if the situation had escalated.
“We can unequivocally say that it was the right decision,” Ezpeleta told the Reuters news agency.
“Obviously, it was normal that the riders showed their concerns, and I think that we mitigated those and confronted them to the best that we ⁠⁠⁠⁠possibly could.”

“It’s just important in today’s day and age to follow official information and real intelligence versus speculation in the media and disinformation, which I think ultimately was what brought a lot of noise around the event itself.”

Several Saudi Arabian sporting events – including football, tennis, golf and cycling – were cancelled or postponed in recent weeks after attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on Riyadh’s international airport last month killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300.
But Ezpeleta said Qatar had not been affected in the same way as its ‌‌‌‌Gulf neighbours and that planning for the race had accelerated after conditions improved in June and July.
Yamaha withdrawal surprised MotoGP

However, Yamaha withdrew from the Qatar Grand Prix citing “company-wide travel restrictions” for the Middle East, with the factory team and the satellite team Prima Pramac not lining up on the grid, reducing the field to 18 riders.
“I can say that the decision surprised us, given the level of detail that was put into the assessment and all the planning,” Ezpeleta said.
“All the questions that Yamaha had were answered. Ultimately, Yamaha is a great partner of the championship historically, and I’m sure they will continue to be,” he added.
“We understand that it wasn’t a decision that was taken easily from their side, but it ⁠⁠⁠⁠is a decision that was surprising to us for sure.”
MotoGP leaves sanctions to FIM
MotoGP had said Yamaha’s non-participation carried ⁠⁠⁠⁠sporting implications, with any consequences to be managed by FIM, the governing body of motorcycle racing.
But Ezpeleta declined to speculate on penalties.
“We just said that we would manage any contractual matters with Yamaha directly and any sporting conversations would be handled by FIM,” he said.

“We continue to say that it’s a disappointment because I think one of the strengths of ⁠⁠⁠⁠MotoGP as a championship is that all the riders, all the teams are committed for the full season,” Ezpeleta added.
“I would say as a rights holder that the teams are committed and obliged to show up at all the events and ⁠⁠⁠⁠all races.”

Yamaha and FIM did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Yamaha’s Moto2 team ⁠⁠⁠⁠travelled to Qatar, with Izan Guevara in a close title fight and sitting second in the championship. He had a technical issue and did not finish.
‘Improve communication’
The episode has also raised questions about how well MotoGP’s management communicates with riders, and Ezpeleta acknowledged the need to improve that relationship with all stakeholders.
“We have to proactively push to improve communication, especially with the teams and the ‌‌‌‌riders because they are obviously the most important part of the championship,” he said.
“We’ve been managing the sport for 35 years and we’ve had situations like this before,” Ezpeleta added, pointing to the 2011 race in Japan held after the Fukushima nuclear disaster.

“There was a lot of controversy at the time, ‌‌‌‌as ‌‌‌‌was now with Qatar, guided by misinformation and speculation, rather than facts,” he said. “We continue to say that this was the right decision.”
Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi won the Qatar Grand Prix, but Ducati’s sprint winner Marc Marquez finished second to establish a 60-point lead in the championship with two rounds left.

items.titel: Russia bars four French figures over expulsion of Xenia Fedorova
items.anriss: One of those targeted says the ban is "recognition" of his work against foreign interference, while the EU accuses the former RT France chief of spreading Kremlin talking points on French television.

absaetze.t: French MPs Sacha Houlié and Arthur Delaporte, along with journalists Ariane Chemin and Paul Gogo, have been banned from entering Russia. The Russian foreign ministry announced the measure on Wednesday in retaliation for France’s expulsion of pro-Kremlin commentator Xenia Fedorova.
ADVERTISEMENT
The four were targeted “because of their involvement in the harassment of Fedorova and their calls for her expulsion”, foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told a press briefing.

Fedorova, the former head of RT France, has since become one of the media faces of the group owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré. Since late July, she has been subject to an expulsion order and an asset freeze in France.
She has also been under EU sanctions since September.
According to a document (source in French) published in the EU’s Official Journal on 24 September, Fedorova is accused of relaying “messages in line with those promoted by the Russian authorities”.

“Xenia Fedorova has notably presented Western and European support for Ukraine as a factor prolonging the war, has described Russia as a country seeking peace while portraying Europe as advocating confrontation, has challenged established facts relating to the illegal transfer and deportation of Ukrainian children, and has disseminated messages depicting European and NATO policies as threats to European security”, the document states.

In its decision, the EU notes that since RT’s broadcasting activities were suspended, Fedorova has appeared regularly on several French media outlets, including the TV channel CNews, the radio station Europe 1 and the newspaper JDD, “through which she has continued to spread these messages to a wide audience in France”.
Who are the figures in the Kremlin’s sights?

Arthur Delaporte is a Socialist MP. Last June, during question time in parliament, he challenged Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over the renewal of Fedorova’s 10-year residence permit. He condemned what he called an “undue and dysfunctional” decision by the prefecture, the local state authority that issues residence permits, and described Fedorova as a “Kremlin propagandist” and an “agent destabilising our country”.
“Are you going to withdraw her permit and launch expulsion proceedings?” he asked.

Sacha Houlié chaired the National Assembly’s law committee from 2022 to 2024 and sits on the parliamentary intelligence delegation. In November 2023, he wrote a report (source in French) on France’s vulnerability to foreign interference, which sets out in detail, over several pages, the methods Moscow favours to extend its influence in France and around the world.
Reacting to the ban on X, Houlié called the decision "recognition of my work against foreign interference in France".
He added that the sanction "invites me to pursue this just commitment to defending France’s fundamental interests".

Houlié is an MP for the Place publique party and a supporter of Raphaël Glucksmann, a candidate in France’s presidential election. Glucksmann has previously said he has been targeted by Russian online “destabilisation” operations.

Ariane Chemin, a senior reporter at the French daily Le Monde, is also a writer. In May, she published The War - These are Proper Nouns, a literary account of the consequences of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Paul Gogo, a journalist who works for several news outlets, lived and worked in Russia for nine years until February 2026. He moved there in 2017, having been based in Ukraine since 2014.

items.titel: A Portuguese group will manufacture components for Swedish Saab fighter jets
items.anriss: A Swedish company announced a partnership with Portuguese industrial group Vangest to produce eight complex parts in Portugal for Gripen E/F fighters. The Swedish jet is among the options to renew the Portuguese Air Force's F-16 fleet.

absaetze.t: Published on 11 November 2026 - 15:44 GMT+1

The Portuguese industrial group Vangest, best known for moulds and plastic parts for various sectors and which has been expanding in the aerospace sector, is going to produce components for Saab's Gripen fighter jets.
ADVERTISEMENT
In a statement, the company explains that the "partnership is part of Saab's work to expand its international manufacturing network and strengthen the production capacity of the Gripen E/F".

The agreement covers the production of eight complex components for Gripen E/F fighter jets at the group's facilities in Marinha Grande, north of Lisbon, and is expected to create "new skilled jobs" in the region.
The Swedish company justifies the partnership with Vangest's "advanced manufacturing capabilities and experience", in an alliance that also has the potential for "expansion in the coming years".

"With Vangest, we are expanding our manufacturing network and strengthening production capacity, while at the same time giving Portuguese industry a concrete role in the Gripen programme," said Johan Segertoft, head of Saab's Gripen business unit, quoted in the company's statement, stressing how the cooperation reaffirms Saab's commitment "to the development of Portugal's aerospace industry".

The value of the deal, including the investment involved, the number of components to be produced or realistic estimates of the number of jobs created, was not specified, nor was the start date for production.

The announcement comes at a time when the launch of the process to renew the Portuguese Air Force's F-16s is awaited. The Gripen fighters are one of the fighter jet models mentioned as a possible purchase option for the Portuguese government.

In Wednesday's statement, the Swedish company says that the selection of its model "would offer more opportunities" to deepen the cooperation now announced, aiming at the "development of Portugal's aerospace and defence industry and strengthening its role in the European defence industrial landscape".

items.titel: Inside Warhound’s plan to engineer a better military working dog
items.anriss: News broke on Oct. 22 that a new startup had raised $200 million to genetically enhance military dogs . The company, Warhound , was launched by billionaire entrepreneurs Ben Lamm , founder of biotech company Colossal Biosciences , and …

absaetze.t: News broke on Oct. 22 that a new startup had raised $200 million to genetically enhance military dogs. The company, Warhound, was launched by billionaire entrepreneurs Ben Lamm, founder of biotech company Colossal Biosciences, and Palmer Luckey, founder of defense technology company Anduril Industries.

The two planned to bring their respective companies’ strengths to the venture. Lamm would apply Colossal’s gene-editing technology to improve the dogs’ physical capabilities, while Luckey would equip them with advanced military equipment. The unusual mission, combined with the founders’ track records, left plenty of questions about what Warhound had planned.

Some speculated that the company intended to create cybernetic superdogs, while others accused its founders of trying to expand an industry that should instead be replaced with robots. But in a news release shared in response to the initial reporting, Warhound described a more grounded goal: rebuilding the domestic supply of dogs for the military, law enforcement and first responders.

In an interview with Military Times, Lamm and Warhound’s co-founder and chief executive David Spirk, who left a senior position at Palantir for the startup, expanded on that statement, discussing the conversations that sparked the mission, the problems they want to address and the product they hope to sell.

Together, they said they want to do more than bring the supply chain to the United States. Their plan includes cloning top-performing dogs, editing genes associated with health problems and introducing standardized training to puppies as young as two weeks old.
A meeting of minds
The idea for Warhound was born out of conversations Lamm had with Luckey beginning around April 2025. They had met at the Moonshots Summit, where they appeared as guest speakers.

“Palmer’s really excited about animals, and he knows I run both the extinction and species conservation company. So, we’re talking about all kinds of stuff, like can you communicate with animals, all these things leveraging technology, and then he started talking to me about the working dog program,” Lamm said.

According to the Defense Department, only about 13% of the dogs trained to become military working dogs come from domestic breeders. Conversely, Warhound estimates that around 80% of the dogs are sourced from overseas, mostly Europe. Lamm described those breeding programs as “a little bit puppy millish.”

Because of supply issues and the time it takes to train a working dog, Warhound estimates that it takes roughly three years before a dog becomes operational. The company said more than half the dogs procured are ultimately deemed unfit for service, meaning the government has to “train roughly 200 dogs today to field 100 working animals tomorrow.”
To address the problem, Lamm said his conversations with Luckey over the past 18 months have evolved from identifying the problem to figuring out how technology could help solve it.
“[Luckey] thought that Anduril could provide a lot of the tech and enabled hardware around this,” Lamm said. “And we could provide the cloning and the genetic engineering.”
The science behind Warhound

Since launching in 2021, Colossal has raised more than $435 million to fund its efforts to revive extinct animals and conserve the genetic material of endangered species. The company’s current valuation is approximately $10.2 billion.

To expand its capabilities, Colossal acquired Texas-based Viagen Pets and Equine last year. Lamm said Viagen has “very high cloning efficiencies … and Warhound will be leveraging Viagen as it relates to dog cloning, which is their core business.”
In 2025, Colossal demonstrated its capabilities by cloning former NFL quarterback Tom Brady’s dog. But cloning and gene editing are distinct processes.

According to the National Institutes of Health, cloning produces a genetically identical copy of an existing animal, whereas gene editing involves directly altering an organism’s DNA to change specific characteristics.

With gene editing, “you’re taking the random chance out of nature,” Lamm said, adding, “Genetic engineering is looking at the genome, finding things that are broken in the genome, wrong in the genome, or could lead to health consequences, and fixing and removing that.”

Gene editing has been used to create specific characteristics in several animal species. Scientists, for example, have used the technique to make pigs more resistant to certain diseases; cattle better suited for hotter environments; and fish grow faster. But its application in dogs remains limited.

In August, the company Kindred Companion Sciences unveiled what it described as the first genetically edited dogs. The biotech company created two hypoallergenic beagles using gene editing to remove a DNA sequence associated with a major dog allergen.
However, Lamm said he does not anticipate significant challenges to applying the technology to working dogs.
“We’re working on stuff that’s like a hundred times more advanced than, you know, a couple dog edits,” he said, referring to his team at Colossal.

“When we made our dire wolves, we made 20 edits, which included edits specifically from dire wolves in those variants that had not existed for over 12,000 years in the genome, so not only can we make edits, but we can even make edits with lost alleles,” he added.
Engineering a better working dog

While the science might not be a problem, Warhound co-founder Spirk said the company’s immediate focus is identifying “the best of the best” dogs and breeds to biobank, as well as developing the company’s “Warhound standard” for training working dogs.

He explained that a wide variety of dogs are used across federal, regional and local agencies. Warhound is working with different government organizations to identify the top-performing animals, though he declined to say which ones.
He said they are “understanding who wants what type of dog, and what the specialized capabilities of that dog are.”
“You can imagine that the dog that we need sitting outside McDill Air Force Base is much different than a dog that somebody’s going to jump out of a helicopter with,” Spirk continued.

Using genetic material collected in the biobank, Warhound scientists will map the animals’ genomes and look for opportunities to edit genes to improve their overall health, wellness and longevity before beginning the cloning process.
“Once the scientists do their magic and make these dogs, we will immediately begin training,” Spirk said, adding that their experts suggest training should begin for puppies as young as two weeks.

The idea behind early training, he explained, is to breed dogs to the highest standard, and then begin acclimating them to the tasks and conditions they’ll be expected to encounter in the field. For example, he said, a dog trained primarily on asphalt might struggle to function on a different surface, such as grass or sand.
“You’re just naturally going to have a better product coming out when we domesticate the production,” Spirk said.
The first Warhounds should be “coming off the line” in about two years, he said.
Once Warhound figures out the right balance of nature and nurture for working dogs, Spirk said the company would like to explore ways to apply its research to the other 98 million dogs in America.
“Nobody’s ever had the resources to do it and to figure it out,” he said, adding, “It’s pretty motivating.”

items.titel: Après Thales, l’allemand Helsing défie l’américain Palantir avec son logiciel de commandement et de contrôle Clarity
items.anriss: Actuellement, faute d’alternative européenne, l’Otan s’approprie le logiciel de commandement et de contrôle [C2] dopé à l’intelligence artificielle MSS NATO [pour Maven Smart System NATO], dérivé du projet Maven, confié par le Pentagone à …

absaetze.t: Actuellement, faute d’alternative européenne, l’Otan s’approprie le logiciel de commandement et de contrôle [C2] dopé à l’intelligence artificielle MSS NATO [pour Maven Smart System NATO], dérivé du projet Maven, confié par le Pentagone à l’américain Palantir. Un tel système vise à compiler et analyser d’énormes quantités de données collectées par une myriade de capteur de toute nature afin que les états-majors puissent mieux identifier d’éventuelles cibles et prendre des décisions plus rapidement.

Plus précisément, quand l’Otan a choisi le MSS NATO, le logiciel de C2 «Arcadia», développé à partir du programme Artemis.IA par Thales et Eviden pour le compte du ministère français des Armées, n’avait pas encore été éprouvé. Ce qui a été récemment fait, à l’occasion des exercices Dacian Fall, Orion 26 et CWIX [Coalition Warrior Interoperability, eXperimentation, eXamination, eXercice].

Schématiquement, Arcadia repose sur une infrastructure «physique», c’est-à-dire des serveurs sécurisés et des «data hub» dits de l’avant, et permet de traiter des données opérationnelles émanant de différentes sources, civiles et militaire, grâce à l’intelligence artificielle.

Puis, en septembre, capitalisant sur l’expérience acquise avec Arcadia et Artemis.IA, Thales a annoncé la mise sur le marché de sa solution multidomaine «Hexaforce», décrite comme étant un «système souverain de commandement militaire augmenté par l’IA», destinée à l’Otan et aux pays alliés.

Reposant sur les technologies de LLM [Large Langage Models] et d’IA agentique, Hexaforce «s’adapte aux conflits de haute intensité dont les besoins de commandement dépassent 100 000 combattants et dont le rythme nécessite un recours massif et raisonné à l’IA», a fait valoir l’industriel français.

Mais un autre acteur vient de se lancer sur ce marché du logiciel de C2. En effet, ce 11 novembre, Helsing, le spécialiste de l’intelligence artificielle de défense établi en Allemagne, a dévoilé «Clarity», une «plateforme de renseignement agentique destinée aux forces armées».

Selon les explications données par l’entreprise, Clarity promet de «traiter simultanément de grands volumes de données, de détecter les menaces et de préparer plus rapidement une réponse fiable». conçue «nativement» autour de l’intelligence artificielle, ce système «s’affranchit» des architectures logicielles actuellement mis en œuvre par les forces armées de l’Otan.

«Clarity traite les données issues de toutes les sources accessibles à une unité, des flux de capteurs et sources ouvertes aux rapports et aux systèmes déjà en service. Elle les recoupe, analyse de grands volumes de données en quelques secondes et détecte les moyens et positions militaires adverses. Un opérateur examine les moyens adverses ainsi identifiés. Clarity prépare ensuite les données nécessaires à l’emploi du système d’armes le mieux adapté», détaille Helsing, qui a sans doute pu nourrir et entraîner ses algorithme d’IA avec les informations collectées en Ukraine.

«Les agents d’IA de Clarity sont conçus pour les besoins militaires. Leurs modèles sont entraînés sur de vastes corpus de données militaires mêlant données réelles représentatives des conditions opérationnelles, données synthétiques générées par l’IA et environnements simulés», explique Helsing. Un telle approche permet ainsi d’imaginer des scénarios que les «données réelles ne documentent pas» et d’anticiper l’évolution des menaces.

Par ailleurs, Helsing insiste sur la «souveraineté» de ce logiciel de C2 dans la mesure où il fonctionne sur «infrastructure appartenant au client», que des modèles d’IA sont développés en Europe, qu’il s’inscrit dans les principes MOSA [Modular Open Systems Approach], qu’il est compatible avec «les systèmes déjà utilisés par les armées» et qu’il se connecte «aux effecteurs de tous les fabricants».

«Les données, les modèles et les opérations restent sous le contrôle du client et Clarity n’appartient à aucun autre acteur», insiste l’entreprise. «Une capacité aussi critique doit être souveraine. Avec Clarity, les forces armées européennes disposent d’un logiciel développé en Europe, déployé sur leur propre infrastructure et sous leur contrôle», a résumé Gundbert Scherf, son vice-PDG et cofondateur.

items.titel: “Free Lyric” Tells the Story of a Young Black Female Rapper Cancelled for Her “Provocative” Lyrics
items.anriss: Free Lyric revisits one of rap culture’s first-ever viral moments: the public shaming of a 17-year-old Black female rapper. Created by BAFTA award-winning filmmaker Cherish ‘Chez’ Oteka, the documentary is now available to watch for free …

absaetze.t: Watch the new documentary by BAFTA award-winning filmmaker Cherish ‘Chez’ Oteka on Field of Vision.
November 11, 2026 — 1 min read

Free Lyric revisits one of rap culture’s first-ever viral moments: the public shaming of a 17-year-old Black female rapper. Created by BAFTA award-winning filmmaker Cherish ‘Chez’ Oteka, the documentary is now available to watch for free on Field of Vision.

In 2011, O.G. Niki released a freestyle detailing her experience of sleeping with six men on one occasion, a sexual confession that shocked the internet. With the rise of social media as the backdrop, Free Lyric follows the journey of Niki and her unique experience of being an early victim of modern-day cancel culture.

Told as an unfolding narrative during the digital era of the early 2010s, this 31-minute short documentary reconstructs the investigations of internet sleuths and online trolls who worked to expose the identity of the girl behind the controversy. Archival footage and social media clips recreate the overwhelming noise of going viral overnight, while dramatized scenes and present-day interviews deliberately challenge the audience’s certainty in what is and isn’t true.

Public understanding of consent and coercion has evolved since the freestyle initially went viral. As Niki prepares a musical comeback for the first time in 15 years, Free Lyric revisits the events that made her infamous with a different understanding of the sexual encounter that once defined her online.

Field of Vision is honored to collaborate on the film’s release with me too. International, who have created a viewer guide to assist audiences in processing the various themes explored in the film. me too. International is a convener, thought leader, and organizer in the global movement to end sexual and gender-based violence.

items.titel: Contemporary Beadworker Ken Williams Jr Awarded Rakow Commission by Corning Museum of Glass
items.anriss: The Corning Museum of Glass selected Northern Arapaho and Cattaraugus Seneca artist Ken Williams Jr as the recipient of the 2026 Rakow Commission . Williams began learning beadwork at an early age on the Cattaraugus Seneca Indian Territory …

absaetze.t: Marking the prize’s 40th year, "I Am the Hungry Cat" is the first Rakow Commission awarded for beadwork.
November 11, 2026 — 2 min read

The Corning Museum of Glass selected Northern Arapaho and Cattaraugus Seneca artist Ken Williams Jr as the recipient of the 2026 Rakow Commission. Williams began learning beadwork at an early age on the Cattaraugus Seneca Indian Territory and later refined his technique alongside master beadworkers from his mother’s Northern Arapaho family.

Widely celebrated for his pictorial beadwork, Williams used the Commission as an opportunity to move beyond functional and wearable forms, creating a standalone wall panel. Utilizing 68 different colors from a range of historic to contemporary made beads, the framed composition features a graphic depiction of the artist’s cat, Valentino, complete with thought bubbles depicting his favorite foods as part of his “Yum Series.” In centering imagery of his cat and favorite foods detailed in bold colors and expressive lines, Williams is actually presenting a self-portrait through the work.

“Beadwork is something I grew up with. It is both familiar and comforting, carrying generations of knowledge passed down through my heritage. To have this traditional art form recognized through the Rakow Commission is deeply meaningful. I’ve always used glass beads to tell stories, but experimenting with a new vehicle and format gave me the freedom to try something fresh and personal. Glass beads allow me to honor my ancestors while pushing my practice toward the future, and I’m thrilled to be able to bring that spirit to CMoG.”— Ken Williams Jr

Now on view in the Museum’s Contemporary Art + Design Gallery, I Am the Hungry Cat, draws inspiration from Pop Art and a vibrant color palette and bridges ancestral artistic traditions with a playful contemporary sensibility, expanding the possibilities of glass as a medium for narrative art.

The Rakow Commission is one of the most prestigious annual awards for artists working in glass and supports the creation of a new work by encouraging artists to venture into technical or conceptual projects that they would have been unable to explore due to financial limitations. The annual program was endowed by the late Dr. and Mrs. Leonard S. Rakow, who were Fellows, benefactors, and dear friends of the Museum.

In its 40th year, the annual award was first presented in 1986, and recipients ranged from emerging to established artists including Te Rongo Kirkwood, Charisse Pearlina Weston, Leo Tecosky, Preston Singletary, Silvia Levenson, Klaus Moje, and Lino Tagliapietra.

items.titel: Art Basel gewährt Galerien 20 Prozent Rabatt
items.anriss: Art Basel gewährt Galerien 20 Prozent Rabatt Daniel Völzke Wed, 11/11/2026 - 15:39

absaetze.t: Die Kunstmesse Art Basel gewährt allen Galerien, die an der diesjährigen Ausgabe in Paris teilgenommen haben, einen Nachlass von 20 Prozent auf ihre Standgebühren
Damit reagiert der Veranstalter auf die vorzeitige Schließung der Messe aus Sicherheitsgründen. Das teilte Art-Basel-Chef Noah Horowitz dem US-amerikanischen Magazin "ARTnews" mit.

Die Art Basel Paris hatte am 24. und 25. Oktober wegen angekündigter Proteste und Sicherheitsbedenken geschlossen. Ursprünglich sollte die Messe bis Sonntag, 26. Oktober, dauern. Für das Wochenende gekaufte Besuchertickets seien bereits erstattet worden. Der Rabatt für die Aussteller werde mit den noch ausstehenden Schlussrechnungen verrechnet. Zusatzkosten etwa für Beleuchtung oder individuelle Standgestaltung seien davon ausgenommen.

Die Entscheidung folgt auf anhaltende Kritik aus der Galerieszene. Das französische Galerienkomitee Comité Professionnel des Galeries d’Art (CPGA), das 57 der 211 Aussteller vertritt, hatte in einem Schreiben vom 28. Oktober eine angemessene Entschädigung gefordert. Der Verband kritisierte insbesondere, dass die Galerien vor der Bekanntgabe der vorzeitigen Schließung nicht konsultiert worden seien. Während die Schließung am Samstag angesichts der angekündigten Proteste weithin als notwendige Sicherheitsmaßnahme angesehen wurde, stieß die Entscheidung, die Messe auch am Sonntag nicht wieder zu öffnen, auf Unverständnis. An diesem Tag waren keine Proteste geplant.

Besonders kleinere und jüngere Galerien seien von den Einnahmeausfällen betroffen, da sie stärker auf Verkäufe am letzten Messewochenende angewiesen seien. Die Art Basel habe sich bewusst gegen Gutscheine für künftige Veranstaltungen und für eine unmittelbare finanzielle Entlastung entschieden, sagte Horowitz. Am 14. Dezember soll ein Treffen zwischen Vertretern der Messe, des CPGA, des französischen Kulturministeriums und des Grand Palais stattfinden, um die Folgen der Schließung und die weitere Zusammenarbeit zu besprechen.

items.titel: Art Basel offers compensation to dealers after early closure of Paris fair due to protests
items.anriss: Exhibitors will receive a 20% discount on booth fees, following a strongly worded letter from France's gallery association to Art Basel

absaetze.t: Art Basel Paris will compensate dealers for the early closure of the fair, held 20-23 October in the Grand Palais, the fair company announced today (11th November), on a French national holiday.

The fair was forced to shut down its Parisian outing two days early because of violent rioting in the French capital. Since then, dealers have been demanding compensation for their lost sales and booth fees. Indeed, soon after the closure the French Comité Professionnel des Galeries d’Art (CPGA) sent a strongly worded letter to the fair director, Karim Crippa. It accused the firm of not consulting with dealers—the CPGA represents 57 of the fair’s 211 exhibitors—and of showing “disrespect, even contempt” for them.

The closure hit the smaller dealers particularly hard, since the biggest galleries tended to make sales on the opening days, whereas the smaller dealers, mainly sited on the upper floor of the Grand Palais, depended on the two weekend days for business. The letter said it expected “concrete proposals” for this compensation.

Now Crippa has responded to the letter, with an offer of a reduction across the board of 20% of booth fees to all participants. He said: “We believe this approach offers a fair and considered way forward, reflecting our appreciation of the partnership we share and our commitment to strengthening it further.”
Philippe Charpentier of Mor Charpentier gallery, who is the president of the CPGA, tells The Art Newspaper that the compensation rate is what the committee expected.

Nonetheless, if one calculates in percentages, the fair was open for three-and-a-half days—it's ultra-VIP Avant-Première timeslot began 3pm on Tuesday 20 October, and the fair closed Friday—instead of the projected five and a half. The fair was therefore shortened by about 36%.

Speaking about the decision to close the fair early, Noah Horowitz, chief executive of Art Basel, tells The Art Newspaper: “We stand by the decision to close. We feel it was in the right interest of all the parties involved. It was a very difficult decision, but we stand by it.”

Asked about the decision to close for the two days—when unrest was only expected on the Saturday—he said: “Given the uncertainty surrounding the impact and the duration of the planned demonstrations and access to the Grand Palais, we simply couldn't be confident that conditions would allow us to reopen safely on Sunday. An event of this size and scale is incredibly complex, and some exhibitors had also expressed serious concerns about leaving artworks unattended in the Grand Palais on the weekend. We concluded that closing the fair early was in the best interests of the art, the staff and ultimately the visitors.”

Horowitz was not prepared to comment on other aspects of the closure, for example questions of insurance or the firm’s relationship with the Grand Palais, for which MCH paid €10.6m to rent the space for seven years in 2022. Horowitz said that MCH, the parent company of the Basel group of art fairs, was "fully committed to delivering the 2027 edition of the fair".
